correction: Believed the sysext plus a domain was enough for browser SSO to corp resources; two more things were required, both learned from comparing the working Ubuntu host. (1) The Unix account doing the SSO must be Entra-authenticated (user-map for a local account), otherwise himmelblaud has no PRT for the caller and the broker loops through interactive auth on every request. (2) apply_policy must be true: it gates both Intune enrollment (run inside a PAM auth, logged by himmelblaud-tasks as apply_intune_policy with an intune_device_id) and aad-tool compliance-check; without it a compliant-device conditional-access tenant answers every PRT-for-token exchange with AADSTS530003 and browsers demand device registration. The Ubuntu host enrolled on 2026-09-08 10:39 while the upstream installer's default apply_policy=true was still in its config; the option was removed afterwards, which is why its periodic check now says 'unavailable' yet resources keep working. The wizard now writes apply_policy = true by default.
evidence: journalctl --user -u himmelblau-broker: 'Silent PRT SSO cookie unavailable; attempting interactive re-auth' loop; himmelblaud: 'Broker method failed for uid 1000: Unable to find account' before the map, 'Failed to exchange PRT for access token: AADSTSError 530003' before apply_policy; Ubuntu journal 2026-09-08 10:39:09 himmelblaud_tasks 'apply_intune_policy ... intune_device_id: dbc6322d-...'; upstream src/daemon/src/daemon.rs gate `if !cfg.get_apply_policy() || cfg.get_oidc_issuer_url().is_some()`; after `--apply-policy` here, `aad-tool compliance-check` printed 'compliance check passed'.
